The glossary of a dictionary

Source: R/dict-tools.R
dict_glossary.Rd

dict_glossary() returns the dictionary as a glossary in Pandoc markdown: a definition list, one entry per key. It is a knit_asis string, so a chunk prints it as markdown with no results: asis:

Usage

dict_glossary(dict = NULL, values = TRUE, sort = TRUE)

Arguments

dict

A dictionary, as read_dict() returns, or NULL. NULL in a knit is the knit's project dictionary; outside a knit it reads dict.yml at the project root. A chapter's dict_local is accepted when given.

values

Whether to show the values: TRUE or FALSE.

sort

Whether to sort the entries by heading, ignoring case (TRUE), or keep the order of the file (FALSE).

Value

A knit_asis string holding the markdown; "" for an empty dictionary.

Details

dict_glossary()

It writes nothing. It is attached in a weft document as claim() and u() are.

An entry is two lines: a heading and : <definition>. The heading is the entry's term as written (markdown), else the key in code; then, when values is TRUE and the entry is a number, quantity, range, year, date or string, its value in parentheses: numbers and quantities through fmt_num() with the decimals written in the file (0.50 prints 0.50; a quantity converted by display: prints as fmt_num() prints it), dates through fmt_date(), so the configuration in force (marks, thousands_from, unit_form, the units: table) applies; outside a knit that is the _weft.yml of the project root, if there is one. A labels or breaks entry shows no value. White space in a definition and in a string value becomes one space (a blank line in a definition starts a paragraph, indented four spaces so that Pandoc keeps it in the same definition); markdown is kept as written. why is never shown. The string ends with a blank line, so text after the chunk is not read as part of the last definition; a chunk adds an HTML comment after it, since knitr drops trailing blank lines.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
writeLines(c("min_samples:",
             "  value: 5",
             "  type: number",
             "  term: minimum sample size",
             "  definition: Fewest samples a site needs."), f)
cat(dict_glossary(read_dict(f)))
#> 
#> minimum sample size (5)
#> :   Fewest samples a site needs.
#>
